source.question: F-12's water cut is near 0.97 and its oil rate has fallen below 200 Sm3/d. What would you recommend doing to the well, and why?

note: Reviewed Oct 31 (2014 decision re-record): fair. An undeclared 36 (months of the WOR window, not a calendar window), a detail value from an uncited result, undeclared 98% and 81%, a claim with 5 numbers; readability asks.

submission.summary: F-12 now makes about 174.6 Sm3/d at 97% water with its choke at 100% and liquid rate flat, so its oil loss is water taking its capacity and the WOR trend shows no oil left before 95% water. If left as is it would make about 42,800 Sm3 in the next 12 months, range 27,000 to 50,700, so a water shut-off in the 3147 to 3161 m blank-pipe gap is the only work that could restore oil, but the last log is 1500 days old and a new log should confirm the depth before the job.

findings.claim: F-12 averaged 174.6 Sm3/d at 97% water on 2014-10-31, down to 173.5 Sm3/d in October.
findings.detail: field_screen as of 2014-10-31 oil_rate 174.6 Sm3/d water_cut 0.9669 uptime 0.9149; production_monthly 2014-10 oil_rate_per_producing_day 173.5 water_cut 0.9665. Alarm water cut above 0.90 since 2013-06-03.

findings.claim: Liquid rate has held near 5,179 Sm3/d while the choke opened to 100% by 2012, so water has taken the well's capacity.
findings.detail: waterflood by_year liquid 5260 Sm3/d choke 100% in 2012, 5136 Sm3/d choke 100% in 2014; monthly 2014-10 liquid 5179 choke 100%. field_voidage replacement_ratio near 1.0 (1.01 in 2014), injection kept pace.

findings.claim: The WOR trend from the last 36 months leaves no oil before 95% water; the 0.95 limit was already passed at 4,296,542 Sm3.
findings.detail: waterflood wor_fit window 2011-11 to 2014-10 months 36 log10_wor_per_million 2.05 intercept -7.54 r2 0.8799 cum_oil_now 4327013 wor_now 28.85; to_limits water_cut 0.95 cum_oil_at_limit 4296542 remaining 0 already_passed true (0.90 at 4138457, 0.80 at 3966892).

findings.claim: On the current decline the well would make about 42,800 Sm3 in the next 12 months, range 27,000 to 50,700.
findings.detail: forecast_production harmonic fit window 2013-09-15 to 2014-10-31 qi 328.85 di 0.895 b 1.0 r2_log 0.7626 uptime 0.8658; cumulative p50 42798 p90 40828 p10 44587 calibrated_band p90 26986 p10 50703 past_forecasts 19 coverage 0.8. Monthly p50 160.81 in 2014-11 falling to 114.8 in 2015-10.

findings.claim: The 2010-09 log showed oil entering from 3,132 to 3,165 m and water from 3,165 to 3,243 m on both passes.
findings.detail: production_log PLT 2010-09 low rate oil comes_in 3132-3165 water 3165-3243 water_cut_at_top 0.608 rate_vs_well 0.28; medium rate oil 3132-3165 water 3165-3243 water_cut 0.628 rate_vs_well 0.55. Perforations 3131-3147, 3161-3180, 3220-3231, 3236-3243, 3250-3257; blank_pipe gaps 3147-3161, 3180-3220 etc. Production 30 days before water_cut 0.6307 oil 2000 Sm3/d.

findings.claim: A plug in the 3,147 to 3,161 m blank-pipe gap would have cut 98% of the water and kept 81% of the oil on that log, leaving water cut near 14%.
findings.detail: PLT 2010-09 at_blank_pipe 3147-3161 low rate below_top oil_share 0.814 water_share 0.981 below_bottom oil 0.768 water 0.925 water_cut_left_above 0.137; medium rate below_top oil 0.752 water 1.0 water_cut_left_above 0.0. Of_flow_left below_top oil 0.812 water 0.972 low rate. Plug already at 3210 on 2010-09-23 isolated lower zones but changed water_cut 0.638 to 0.676 oil 1850 to 1612, so ineffective.

findings.claim: That log is 1500 days old and water cut has risen from 63% to 97% since, so confirm with a new log before work; no new perforations above are needed.
findings.detail: since_survey latest 2010-09-22 days 1500 water_cut_then 0.6307 water_cut_now 0.9658. Gap 3147-3161 lies between existing perforations 3131-3147 and 3161-3180, so oil above plug remains accessed. Other gaps 3180-3220 and 3231-3236 are already_isolated by the 3210 plug and cut 0-1% of oil and 1-2% of water left. Recommended depth 3155 m within blank pipe gives water_cut_left_above 0.154 low rate 0.104 medium rate.

result.summary: 30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.05 on 2009-10-31, 21 months after first oil.
water_cut shifts around 2010-03-28: weekly mean 0.043 -> 0.689 (+0.65) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 0.33 -> 0.42 (+0.09).
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.5 on 2010-06-04, 28 months after first oil.

oil_rate shifts around 2010-07-18: weekly mean 4,050 -> 1,307 (-68%) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 2,352 -> 1,838 (-22%); the choke stayed about the same (54 -> 51%).
Shut in for 12 days from 2010-08-16. Oil rate 1,821 -> 2,000 Sm3/d (+10%) after restart. Same time as F-14 (field-wide).

bhp_bar reads 0 on 1408 days from 2010-10-12 to 2014-10-31 while the well kept flowing on 1229 days (880,456 Sm3 oil): a sensor failure, not a pressure collapse. Last good reading: 253.9 on 2010-10-11.
Shut in for 10 days from 2011-06-21. Oil rate 1,144 -> 1,364 Sm3/d (+19%) after restart. Same time as F-14 (field-wide).
Shut in for 20 days from 2011-10-16. Oil rate 955 -> 1,158 Sm3/d (+21%) after restart. Same time as F-14 (field-wide).
Shut in for 11 days from 2012-01-03. Oil rate 1,063 -> 1,028 Sm3/d (-3%) after restart. Same time as F-14 (field-wide).
water_cut shifts around 2012-02-12: weekly mean 0.689 -> 0.912 (+0.22) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 0.78 -> 0.83 (+0.05).
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.8 on 2012-02-14, 48 months after first oil.

oil_rate shifts around 2012-03-11: weekly mean 1,307 -> 625 (-52%) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 931 -> 864 (-7%); the choke stayed about the same (100 -> 97%).
Shut in for 46 days from 2012-08-14. Oil rate 691 -> 728 Sm3/d (+5%) after restart. Same time as F-14 (field-wide).
Shut in for 13 days from 2013-03-12. Oil rate 531 -> 572 Sm3/d (+8%) after restart.

oil_rate shifts around 2013-09-15: weekly mean 625 -> 228 (-63%) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 521 -> 356 (-32%); the choke was cut at the same time (100 -> 87%), so part of the change is the operator's, not the reservoir's.
Shut in for 9 days from 2014-05-16. Oil rate 194 -> 193 Sm3/d (-1%) after restart.

summaries.summary: Skidded rig to F-12. Made up 36" hole opener BHA and RIH with same to 85 m MD.
Made FG check of TDS. Serviced TDS. RIH with 36" hole opener. Drilled 36" hole section from 145 m to 250 m MD.

Drilled 36" hole section to TD at 258 m MD. Displaced well to 1,40 sg mud. POOH with 36" hole opener BHA. Rigged up for running 30" conductor. Ran 30" conductor. Started running 4 3/4" cement stinger inside conductor.
Dismounted and mounted tension cylinders. RIH with production riser to 100 m MD.

RIH with PR tensioner joint. MU PR landing stand, RIH and landed riser. Locked TBC connector. Waited on Simens rig ESD test. Pressure tested PR to 200 bar. Install centralizer and boat collision stool on centralizer deck.
MU tensioner ring assembly. POOH and LD PR RT. Installed hatch on F-12 and suspended operation to F-7.
Skidded rig from F-12 to F-15. Changed wire on port aft crane big hook.
Built scaffolding at the well head deck and in the moon pool. Installed surface riser, BOP and tension cylinders.
Nippled up slick jnt, diverter and torqued up the BOP. RIH and installed the Bowl Protector at 20.9 m. Retrieved the Annulus Insert at 139.9 m. Retrieved the Bowl Protector.
RIH with 10 3/4" Tie Back and made up into sub sea well. Pressure tested Tie Back connector to 345 bars. Attempted to lock the Surface hanger, with the Adjustment sub.
Retrieved landing string. Installed BPV. Nippled down BOP and Riser. Installed dart in BPV. Terminated control lines. Installed extension spool.
Installed the WH extension spool, Xmas tree and the production Co-flex hose.
Leak tested X-mas tree connections to 30/345 bars 5/10 min. Lined up and leak tested production line 50/180 bars 5/10 min. Inflow tested LMV and HMV against BPV.
Sent firing command to E-Fire firing head in TCP guns and perforated well from 3130 to 3281 mMDRT.

Handed well over from Production. RU HMV and DHSV to local control panel. Installed test and bleed manifold on to XMT KWV. Performed line test from KWV to cmt unit. Attempted to leak tested XMT cross to 30/200 bar for 5/10 min.

Operated and greased up leaking PWV. Leak tested XMT cross to 30/200 bar for 5/10 min. Installed WL BOP and riser on XMT. Tested shear seals on WL BOP. Installed combination toolstring in riser. MU lubricator. Leak test WL riser, BOP and lubricator. Equalize and open HMV and DHSV. RIH with combination toolstring and tagged TCP guns at 3260.5 m. Performed correlation log in 7" liner. POOH and prepared for inflow test of HMV.

Inflow tested HMV to 81-5 bar/10 min. Broke lubricator and LD toolstring. Installed PLT toolstring in riser. MU lubricator and leak tested at in-situ sub. Equalized and opened HMV. RIH with PLT toolstring on 7/16" EWL from surface to 2929 m. Performed stationary logging at DHPG depth. Continued RIH from 2929 m to 3030 m to perform shut-in station logs and 4 PLT tool calibration passes in the interval 3030 m to 3255 m MD. Bean up well to 4500 Sm3/day. Performed station logs and 4 high rate flowing PLT passes in the interval 3030 m to 3255 m MD. Choked back flow to 3000 Sm3/day. Performed station logs and 4 medium rate flowing PLT passes in the interval 3030 m to 3255 m MD.

Choked back flow to 1500 Sm3/day. Performed station logs and 4 low rate flowing PLT passes in the interval 3030 m to 3255 m MD. Shut-in well. POOH with PLT toolstring. Inflow tested DHSV, HMV and MMV for handover. BO lubricator and LD toolstring. LD lubricator. RD and LD WL riser.

RD BOP from XMT. Leak test XMT cross, KWV and tree cap. Hand well over to Mærsk Production. Cleared and cleaned rig floor of remaining WL equipment. Transferred operation to F-99 for PRS-and 5-yearly BOP classification.
Waited on access to well. Took over well. Rigged up WL riser and BOP.

RU WL equipment. Installed BHA into lubricator. RIH with PLT. Performed spinner calibration. Performed depth correlation with GR/CCL. Took stationary reading at 2929 m. Ran PLT shut in pass. Took stationary readings. Beaned up well. Waited for stable flow.

Waited for stable flow aprox. 5050 Sm3/d with PLT at 3080 m. Attempted to RIH at various speed. No-go. Reduced flow rate to 3000 Sm3/d. Took stationary readings at 3080, 3155, 3200 and 3250 m. Logged flowing passes between 3030 and 3250 m, down at 40 m/min and up at 10/20/30/40 m/min. Reduced flow rate to 1500 Sm3/d. Logged flowing passes between 3000 and 3250 m, down at 40 m/min and up at 10/20/30/40 m/min. Unable to log down on both flowing rates at 10/20/30 m/min. POOH with PLT. Changed tool string. RIH with 5,72" EVO bridge plug at 800 m.
Installed 5,72" EVO bridge plug at 3210 m mid element. RD wireline pressure control equipment and handed well over to production department.

result.note: Daily reports exist for drilling and for work on the well (wireline, plugs, perforations, production logs), not for days of normal production. A job's date is the day the work was done; kind is drilling, completion, workover (work on a producing or injecting well) or abandonment. Ask for one day to see every operation line.

result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. The water cuts in to_limits are reference points, not an economic limit: the data holds no costs or prices, so remaining_oil_sm3 says how much oil is left before each, not whether it pays. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.

report_says.quote: ~83% of oil produced from the upper 2 completions, the rest from the lower 3

surveys.read_from: LAS files of the interpreted log (Well_logs_pr_WELL/15_9-F-12/10.PRODUCTION LOGS/PLT Sept 2010)

result.note: A production log measures the flow passing each depth while the well flows; going up, it grows past each zone that produces. A share at a depth is the part of the pass's oil or water entering below that depth (1 at the bottom of the well's inflow, 0 above the top zone). comes_in_from_m to to_m holds 90% of each phase's inflow. Only shares are given: the files' rates have no units, and the plots' are downhole volumes. A plug set at a depth shuts off what enters below it: the shares below say what it could remove, not what it did; plugs_set gives what each plug already set did to the well (water cut and oil before and after). A bridge plug is set in blank pipe, never inside a perforated interval (inside_perforation_m names the interval a depth falls in; blank_pipe_m lists the gaps, and each pass's at_blank_pipe gives the shares below the top and the bottom of every gap: the depths a plug can actually be set at). A plug set after a survey (its plugs_set_since) already shut off what entered below it: on that log a depth or gap at or below it is already_isolated (a plug there cuts nothing new), and of_flow_left gives what a shallower plug would cut as a share of the flow left above the old plug. water_cut_left_above is the water cut of the flow entering above a depth on that pass, what a plug there would leave flowing (for a gap, a plug anywhere in it): compare it with the well's water cut now to say what a plug would change. rate_vs_well is the pass's surface rate over the well's own in the month before: a pass run far below it may weight the zones differently. since_survey says how old the latest log is and how far the water cut has moved since: an old log may no longer show where the water enters, and a new one would settle it. Each survey's passes were run at several surface rates. A survey read off pictures carries the checks of that reading.

result.calibrated_band_note: P90-P10 from the errors of 19 forecasts made the same way from earlier dates on data up to then; use it for confidence, the bootstrap band above only reflects the fit's scatter. With 19 past forecasts such a range holds about 80% of outcomes. 18 of them were made before this fit window began, in another regime, so the band may be too narrow.
result.p50_by_model_note: The P50 each Arps model gives on this window: when they differ widely, the choice of model drives the forecast as much as the data does.
result.note: P90 = low case, P10 = high case. Volumes = rate x historical uptime.
